hook.pin_description: At Taksim Metro and Eminonu Ferry, anyone offering unsolicited help with the Istanbulkart machine will load 200 lira on your card, charge 350 in cash, and pocket 150 — or swap the loaded card for a near-depleted one at handover. The English menu is on the first screen. From Tabiji's Istanbul scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a man near the Istanbulkart machine at Taksim Metro stepping toward an arriving tourist with luggage, saying the machine is confusing and offering to help.

lesson.lesson: Operate the machine yourself. Verify at the turnstile.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Istanbul rule: operate the Istanbulkart machine yourself
lesson.pin_description: The card costs 100 lira plus your chosen load and the English menu starts at screen one. Verify the balance the second the card is in your hand — it shows on the turnstile reader. If wrong, ask the IETT kiosk staff to check the transaction history, or call 153. More Istanbul scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist tapping an Istanbulkart at a Taksim Metro turnstile and reading the correct balance off the gate display, with the takeaway 'Operate the machine yourself. Verify at the turnstile.'

scams.location: Grand Bazaar (Kapali Carsi), Spice Bazaar (Misir Carsisi)

stacked.headline: The Istanbul carpet that walks from 8,000 lira to 3,000.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Grand Bazaar carpet scam: 8,000 lira opens, drops to 3,000 at the door
stacked.pin_description: In the lanes between Beyazit and Nuruosmaniye gates, sellers seat tourists 45-90 minutes with apple tea and a grandmother story. The first carpet is 8,000 lira; "for you, friend, 3,000" arrives when you stand. Comparable rugs in Fatih shops outside the tourist zone go for 1,200-1,800. The dramatic drop is the trap. From the Tabiji Istanbul Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of a Grand Bazaar aggressive upsell between the Beyazit and Nuruosmaniye gates: a seller invites a tourist couple in for apple tea, they sit while kilims are stacked, the price walks from 8,000 to 3,000 lira when they stand to leave, and the takeaway shows the couple leaving the bazaar for fixed-price shops in Fatih.

hook.hook: "For you, friend, 3,000 — my cost price." Stand and walk.
hook.pin_title: Grand Bazaar "my cost price" line is still double the Fatih street rate
hook.pin_description: In the Grand Bazaar's covered lanes, an 8,000-lira opening that walks to 3,000 when you stand still doubles the 1,200-1,800 lira street rate in Fatih. The 62% "saving" is theatre against an inflated anchor. Stand up, say "not today." From Tabiji's Istanbul scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Grand Bazaar carpet seller in the Kapali Carsi covered lanes pitching one last price to a tourist couple who are starting to stand.

lesson.lesson: You owe nothing for tea. Stand and leave.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Grand Bazaar rule: you owe nothing for tea, stand and leave
lesson.pin_description: For any Grand Bazaar item over 2,000 lira, ask the seller to demonstrate knot count, dye type, and weaving region. A real seller can do all three. The Grand Bazaar Merchants' Association at grandbazaaristanbul.org lists licensed vendors. Fixed-price shops in Fatih are the better buy. More Istanbul scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist couple walking out of a Grand Bazaar carpet shop into the covered lane, with the takeaway 'You owe nothing for tea. Stand and leave.'

stacked.headline: The Istanbul airport taxi that runs gece rate at noon.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: IST airport taxi scam: gece night rate at 2 PM doubles a 300-lira fare
stacked.pin_description: At Istanbul Airport (IST) and Sabiha Gokcen (SAW), drivers toggle the meter to gece (night rate, double) during daytime or skip the O-3 highway for the coastal route. Real IST-Sultanahmet is 250-350 lira; tourists pay 450-600. Book BiTaksi, InDriver, or Uber inside arrivals, or take Havaist bus for 140 lira. From the Tabiji Istanbul Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Istanbul Airport taxi meter trick at IST: a tourist couple with luggage boards a rank cab, the meter shows gece night rate at 2 PM, the driver detours onto the coastal road claiming the highway is closed, and the takeaway shows the tourist booking BiTaksi inside the arrivals hall instead.

hook.hook: "Meter? Of course, sir — gece rate." Reset before you move.
hook.pin_title: Istanbul Airport: gece (night rate) at 2 PM is the meter trick
hook.pin_description: Gece (night rate) on an Istanbul taxi meter applies only midnight to 6 AM. If you see it during daytime at IST or Sabiha Gokcen, point at it and tell the driver to reset before the car moves. Day rate is gunduz. The official IST-Sultanahmet fare is 250-350 lira on the O-3 highway. From Tabiji's Istanbul scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of an Istanbul airport rank taxi meter close-up showing the gece night rate indicator illuminated, with the driver behind the wheel waiting for the tourist to notice.

lesson.lesson: Gece is night only. Take Havaist or BiTaksi.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Istanbul airport rule: gece is night only, use Havaist or BiTaksi
lesson.pin_description: Verify the meter shows gunduz (day rate) before the wheels move at IST or SAW. Photograph the start reading and name every banknote out loud. Havaist bus to Taksim is 140 lira and runs every 30 minutes. The IBB fare calculator at ibb.gov.tr posts the official ranges. More Istanbul scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist boarding the Havaist airport bus at Istanbul Airport with luggage, looking at a 140-lira fare sign, with the takeaway 'Gece is night only. Take Havaist or BiTaksi.'

scams.location: Antalya Airport arrivals between Domestic and International terminals, Kaleici Old Town taxi stands, Lara Beach resort pickups, late-night rides from bars in the marina area

stacked.headline: The Antalya taxi that bills 55 euros for a 170-lira ride.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Antalya airport taxi scam: 170 TL becomes 55 euros between terminals
stacked.pin_description: At Antalya Airport, the same company quotes 170 TL from the domestic terminal but 55 EUR (about 306 TL) from the international terminal — for a 100-meter ride. Drivers refuse the meter, quote in euros, or run gece night rate by day. Real airport-to-Kaleici is 350-500 TL. Use the official outdoor rank or BiTaksi only. From the Tabiji Antalya Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of Antalya Airport taxi meter manipulation: a driver approaches a tourist inside arrivals offering a ride, the meter is off and the fare is quoted at 55 euros instead of the 170 TL on the metered price, the route detours through deserted Lara Beach side streets at night, and the takeaway shows the tourist booking BiTaksi at the licensed outdoor stand.

hook.hook: "Taxi? Fixed price, fifty-five euros." Walk to the meter rank.
hook.pin_title: Antalya Airport: a euro quote is the meter-manipulation tell
hook.pin_description: Any Antalya driver pricing in euros instead of lira is setting his own exchange rate — 55 EUR for a 170 TL ride is a documented case. Drivers who approach you inside arrivals are unlicensed. Walk to the official outdoor rank, insist on gunduz (day) rate, or open BiTaksi. From Tabiji's Antalya scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of an unlicensed driver inside Antalya Airport arrivals approaching a tourist with a wheeled suitcase, offering a fixed price of fifty-five euros.

lesson.lesson: Pay in lira. Insist on the meter.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Antalya rule: pay in lira and insist on the meter
lesson.pin_description: Airport-to-Kaleici is 350-500 TL and airport-to-Lara is 250-400 TL on the meter (2025 prices). Refuse euros, refuse "broken meter," refuse drivers approaching inside the terminal. Ask for a makbuz (receipt) and report overcharging to 155. More Antalya scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at the official outdoor Antalya Airport taxi stand pointing at the meter showing gunduz day rate, with the takeaway 'Pay in lira. Insist on the meter.'

scams.location: Marina restaurants along Antalya harbor, Kaleici Old Town tourist restaurants, Lara Beach resort strip eateries, rooftop dining spots near Hadrian's Gate

stacked.headline: The Antalya restaurant where 150-TL dishes appear at 350 on the bill.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Antalya restaurant scam: 150-TL menu becomes 350 on the bill in Kaleici
stacked.pin_description: Around the Antalya marina, Kaleici Old Town, and Hadrian's Gate, restaurants charge 2-3x the menu price, add fake "tax" lines, and bring un-ordered bread or meze that hits the bill. Photograph the menu before ordering, ask if bread, water, and service are extra, and threaten to call 155 if the bill is wrong. From the Tabiji Antalya Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of an Antalya Kaleici restaurant bill inflation scam: a tout invites tourists in from the street with promises of a discount, the waiter brings unordered bread and meze to the table, the bill arrives with 150-TL dishes priced at 350 plus a fake tax line, and the takeaway shows the tourist photographing the original menu beside the bill.

hook.hook: "Special discount tonight, my friend!" Skip the tout-front restaurant.
hook.pin_title: Antalya "special discount" tout fronts a 2-3x bill on the way out
hook.pin_description: In Kaleici and the marina, restaurants with a tout on the street charge 30-50% more on the bill than the menu shows. 150-TL dishes appear at 350 lira; phantom "tax" lines and unordered bread inflate it further. Photograph the menu before ordering. From Tabiji's Antalya scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of an Antalya marina restaurant tout in a vest aggressively waving a tourist couple toward an empty table, promising a special discount.

lesson.lesson: Photograph the menu before you order.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Antalya rule: photograph the menu before you order
lesson.pin_description: Compare every Antalya bill line by line against the photographed menu. Ask before sitting whether bread, water, and service are extra. Avoid restaurants with street touts; check Google reviews first. Refuse to pay an inflated bill — 155 (Tourist Police) usually resolves it on the spot. More Antalya scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist seated at an Antalya Kaleici restaurant holding a phone showing a photo of the menu beside the printed bill, with the takeaway 'Photograph the menu before you order.'

scams.location: Kaleici Old Town narrow streets, shops near Hadrian's Gate, tourist markets near the Clock Tower, carpet galleries along Ataturk Caddesi

stacked.headline: The Antalya "125-year-old rug" appraised at 100 dollars.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Antalya carpet scam: $5,000 "125-year-old rug" later appraised at $100
stacked.pin_description: In Kaleici Old Town near Hadrian's Gate and the Clock Tower, touts pull tourists into shops selling "125-year-old" carpets that are recent Chinese machine-mades. Travelers report paying $2,000-5,000 for rugs later appraised at $100-300, with worthless in-house "certificates." Pay by credit card or skip it. From the Tabiji Antalya Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of an Antalya Kaleici carpet pressure sale near Hadrian's Gate: a tout invites a tourist couple into the family shop for tea, the seller unrolls a rug claimed to be a 125-year-old silk handmade, the price climbs from initial quote toward 5,000 dollars while the rug is actually a Chinese machine-made worth 100, and the takeaway shows the couple walking out past the Clock Tower.

hook.hook: "125 years old, hand-knotted silk — for you, friend." It's machine-made.
hook.pin_title: Antalya Kaleici "125-year-old silk" is a Chinese machine-made fake
hook.pin_description: In Kaleici and along Ataturk Caddesi, "hand-knotted antique silk" carpets pitched by touts are typically Chinese machine-made fakes. Tourists report $2,000-5,000 sales later appraised at $100-300. The shop's certificate of authenticity is printed in-house. From Tabiji's Antalya scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of an Antalya Kaleici carpet seller near Hadrian's Gate unrolling a red rug for a tourist couple, claiming it is 125 years old and hand-knotted silk.

lesson.lesson: Tea is not a contract. Pay by credit card.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Antalya rule: tea is not a contract, pay by credit card
lesson.pin_description: Never follow a Kaleici street tout into a carpet shop. If you really want a rug, research a verified dealer, get an independent appraisal, and pay by credit card so you can dispute fake-silk fraud. Shipping the rug home removes your last chance to inspect it. More Antalya scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist couple walking past a Kaleici carpet shop near the Clock Tower without entering, with the takeaway 'Tea is not a contract. Pay by credit card.'

scams.location: Online listings for Kaleici boutique hotels, Lara Beach apartment rentals, Belek golf resort area, Kemer coastal villas

stacked.headline: The Antalya villa listed 30-50% under market that doesn't exist.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Antalya booking fraud: 30-50% below-market villa, bank-transfer only
stacked.pin_description: Fraudulent listings for Kaleici boutique hotels, Lara Beach apartments, and Kemer villas appear on social media at 30-50% below market. The "host" demands bank transfer or Western Union, sends a convincing fake confirmation, then disappears. Book through Booking.com, Airbnb, or Hotels.com only — never wire money. From the Tabiji Antalya Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of Antalya accommodation booking fraud for a Kaleici boutique hotel: a tourist sees a villa listed 40% below market on social media, the host requests a bank transfer instead of a platform booking, the tourist arrives in Antalya to find the address does not exist, and the takeaway shows the tourist booking through Booking.com instead.

hook.hook: "Bank transfer only — high demand, book today." Walk away.
hook.pin_title: Antalya "bank transfer only" villa listing is the booking-fraud tell
hook.pin_description: Any Antalya accommodation host who insists on bank transfer or Western Union, refuses a video call, and pressures you to book a 30-50% under-market villa is running booking fraud. The address often doesn't exist. Stick to Booking.com, Airbnb, or Hotels.com with refund policies. From Tabiji's Antalya scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at a laptop looking at a Kemer coastal villa listing on social media with a host's message demanding bank transfer payment for a high-demand booking.

lesson.lesson: Never wire money for an Antalya rental.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Antalya rule: never wire money for a rental
lesson.pin_description: Cross-reference any Antalya rental address on Google Maps and Street View before paying. Read recent reviews from multiple months. Call the property using a number you found independently, not the one in the listing. Booking.com, Airbnb, and Hotels.com refund fraudulent listings. More Antalya scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at a laptop verifying a Lara Beach apartment address on Google Street View before booking, with the takeaway 'Never wire money for an Antalya rental.'

scams.location: Konyaalti Beach, Lara Beach public area, Kemer resort beaches, Belek coastal strip

stacked.headline: The Antalya jet ski with a $30 "fuel deposit" you never see again.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Antalya jet ski scam: $50-80 ad price plus $30-50 "fuel deposit" never returned
stacked.pin_description: On Konyaalti, Lara, Kemer, and Belek beaches, jet skis advertised at $50-80 add a non-refundable $30-50 "fuel deposit," start the timer at the safety briefing, or claim $200-500 in fake post-ride damage. Book through your hotel or a licensed operator with posted prices. Pay by credit card. Photograph equipment first. From the Tabiji Antalya Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of an Antalya watersport equipment bait and switch on Konyaalti Beach: a beach operator quotes a fifty-dollar jet ski price, the tourist pays plus a thirty-dollar fuel deposit and is told the timer started at the safety briefing, the operator demands two hundred dollars for fake damage after the ride, and the takeaway shows the tourist photographing the equipment before signing.

hook.hook: "Fuel deposit is fifty euros — refundable." It isn't.
hook.pin_title: Antalya jet ski "refundable fuel deposit" never gets refunded
hook.pin_description: Antalya beach jet ski operators on Konyaalti and Lara quote $50-80 then add a $30-50 "fuel deposit" that's never returned, or claim $200-500 damage from pre-existing wear. No insurance, no posted prices, cash only. Book through a hotel-vetted licensed operator. From Tabiji's Antalya scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of an Antalya beach jet ski operator on Lara Beach handing a tourist a clipboard, demanding fifty euros as a fuel deposit on top of the advertised price.

lesson.lesson: Photograph the gear. Pay by card. Get a written quote.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Antalya rule: photograph the gear, pay by card, written quote first
lesson.pin_description: Get a written quote covering fuel, equipment, and insurance before any Antalya watersport. Pay by credit card for dispute protection. Photograph the jet ski or parasail before use as evidence against fake-damage claims. Confirm a Turkish tourism license is displayed. More Antalya scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist on Konyaalti Beach photographing a jet ski before riding it, holding a written quote in the other hand, with the takeaway 'Photograph the gear. Pay by card. Get a written quote.'

scams.scam_name: Bar Drink Spiking and Bill Inflation
scams.location: Bar Street (Barlar Sokagi) in Kaleici, clubs near the marina, late-night bars in Lara Beach hotel zone, rooftop bars targeting solo male tourists

stacked.headline: The Antalya "let's have a drink" bar bill that hits $2,000.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Antalya bar scam: "let's have a drink" ends at $500-2,000 with bouncers
stacked.pin_description: On Bar Street (Barlar Sokagi) in Kaleici and clubs near the marina, a friendly local invites a solo male tourist for drinks; the bill arrives at $500-2,000 and bouncers turn threatening. The drink-spiking variant ends with stolen wallet, phone, and watch. Pick your own venue, watch the pour, pay per round. From the Tabiji Antalya Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Antalya bar drink spiking and bill inflation scam in Kaleici: a friendly local invites a solo male tourist to a Bar Street venue, drinks arrive without a visible price menu, the bill reaches two thousand dollars with bouncers blocking the exit, and the takeaway shows the tourist ordering a sealed bottle at a Google-reviewed bar instead.

hook.hook: "Let's have a drink — I know a place." Pick your own bar.
hook.pin_title: Antalya "let's have a drink" pitch ends at a $500-$2,000 bill
hook.pin_description: On Bar Street in Kaleici, a stranger steering you toward a specific bar is the front of a $500-2,000 bill with bouncers at the exit. The drink-spiking variant in late-night Kaleici and Lara bars ends with stolen wallet, phone, and watch. Pick your own bar from Google reviews. From Tabiji's Antalya scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a friendly local on Bar Street in Kaleici approaching a solo male tourist with an arm gesture, suggesting they go to a specific bar he knows.

lesson.lesson: Pick your own bar. Watch the pour. Pay per round.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Antalya rule: pick your own bar, watch the pour, pay per round
lesson.pin_description: Choose Antalya bars from Google reviews and visible foot traffic, not a stranger's pick. Order sealed bottles and open them yourself. Pay each round on arrival rather than running a tab. Go out in groups. Share live location. If the bill is wrong, dial 155. More Antalya scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at a Kaleici bar opening a sealed bottle himself while paying for the round on arrival, with the takeaway 'Pick your own bar. Watch the pour. Pay per round.'

scams.location: Hotel lobbies and reception areas across Marmaris, particularly in budget and mid-range hotels in the Icmeler area and along the Siteler strip

stacked.headline: The Marmaris fake Jet2 rep who books £320 of excursions that never happen.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Marmaris fake Jet2 holiday rep scam: £320 cash for excursions that vanish
stacked.pin_description: In Marmaris and Icmeler hotel lobbies, a man with a Jet2 or TUI clipboard pitches a 'welcome meeting' and sells boat trips, Dalyan mud baths, and Ephesus tours for £80 per person cash. Jet2 has no rep in Marmaris — the trips never materialise. Verify reps in your booking paperwork or the operator app. From the Tabiji Marmaris Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of a Marmaris hotel-lobby fake holiday rep scam: a man in a Jet2 polo invites a family to a 'welcome meeting' in the Icmeler reception, presents a printed excursion sheet for boat trips and Ephesus tours at £80 per person, the family pays £320 cash with no receipt, and the takeaway shows a tourist on the Jet2 app verifying the real rep is not in Marmaris.

hook.hook: "Welcome meeting at 10? I'm your Jet2 rep." Verify in the app first.
hook.pin_title: Marmaris hotel lobby: "I'm your Jet2 rep" with a clipboard is the pitch
hook.pin_description: If a man with a Jet2 or TUI clipboard greets you in your Marmaris or Icmeler hotel lobby and invites you to a 'welcome meeting,' he is not your operator's rep. Real reps are listed in your pre-departure paperwork. Verify on the operator app before paying any cash. From Tabiji's Marmaris scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a smartly dressed man in a Jet2 polo holding a branded clipboard greeting a British family in the reception of a Marmaris hotel and inviting them to a 'welcome meeting' for excursions.

lesson.lesson: Verify any rep in the operator app first.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Marmaris rule: verify any holiday rep in the operator app first
lesson.pin_description: Real Jet2 and TUI reps in Marmaris are named in your pre-departure paperwork and in the operator app. Anyone in the hotel lobby pitching cash-only excursions with no printed receipt is freelance — book through TripAdvisor-reviewed operators or the official app instead. More Marmaris scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist in a Marmaris hotel lobby holding her phone open to the Jet2 app showing 'no rep assigned to this hotel,' with the takeaway 'Verify any rep in the operator app first.'

stacked.headline: The Marmaris Bar Street £58 bill for four vodkas and a hidden 500-lira service charge.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Marmaris Bar Street scam: 1,200 lira bill + 500 lira hidden service charge
stacked.pin_description: On Marmaris Bar Street (Barlar Sokagi), promoters lure you in with 'free entry' deals. The bill at closing is 1,200 lira for four vodka mixers plus an undisclosed 500-lira service charge — and 14 venues were shut down for harassment. Pay per round, never run a tab, never accept a drink from strangers. From the Tabiji Marmaris Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of a Marmaris Bar Street bill-inflation and drink-spiking scam: a promoter on Barlar Sokagi shouts 'free entry, first drink free' to a couple, the bartender pours four vodkas with no posted prices, the closing bill arrives at 1,200 lira plus a 500-lira service charge, and the takeaway shows the couple keeping a hand on each drink and paying per round.

hook.hook: "Free entry, first drink free!" Pay per round, not on a tab.
hook.pin_title: Marmaris Bar Street "free entry, first drink free" runs a 1,200 lira tab
hook.pin_description: If a promoter on Marmaris Bar Street pitches 'free entry, first drink free' and waves you inside without a posted price list, the closing tab will be 1,200 lira plus a hidden 500-lira service charge. Pay per round, keep your drink in hand, never accept a drink from strangers. From Tabiji's Marmaris scam guide.

lesson.lesson: Pay per round and keep your drink in hand.

lesson.pin_title: Marmaris nightlife rule: pay per round and keep your drink in hand
lesson.pin_description: The Marmaris Bar Street tab inflates after the third round and a 500-lira 'service charge' is added at closing. Pay per round, keep your drink in your hand at all times, and refuse drinks from strangers who join the table. Check TripAdvisor reviews for the specific bar before going. More Marmaris scams from Tabiji.

stacked.pin_description: On Marmaris harbour day-boats, the crew confiscates your food and water 'for safety,' then sells 50-lira water and 100-lira fries while the cocktail poster items are 'not available.' hook.hook: "We have to take your food and water — safety reasons." Refuse to board.

hook.pin_description: If a Marmaris harbour day-boat crew confiscates your cooler bag 'for safety,' the 600-lira 'all-inclusive' was a bait-and-switch — water is 50 lira and the cocktail poster is 'not available.' Get written confirmation of what's included before paying, or pick a TripAdvisor-vetted operator at 15-35 EUR per person. From Tabiji's Marmaris scam guide.

lesson.pin_title: Marmaris boat rule: get "all-inclusive" itemised in writing first
lesson.pin_description: The Marmaris all-inclusive boat scam works because nobody itemises the meals, drinks, or snorkel kit before boarding. stacked.pin_description: Vendors at the Library of Celsus, Great Theatre, and lower gate exit hold up 'authentic Roman coins discovered yesterday' for €5-€50. They are modern Turkish replicas chemically aged in industrial volume — and even genuine antiquities cannot leave Turkey under Law 2863. Walk past without eye contact. From the Tabiji Turkey Scam Survival Guide.

hook.pin_description: At the Library of Celsus and Great Theatre, vendors offer 'Roman coins found yesterday' for €5-€50. Genuine Roman coins from licensed dealers cost €500+; these are mass-produced replicas. Even real antiquities are blocked at the airport under Turkey Law 2863. Walk past, no eye contact. From Tabiji's Turkey scam guide.

Engaging with site vendors marks you for follow-up and rare fake-police 'antiquity smuggling' shake-downs at the lower gate. More Ephesus scams from Tabiji.

scams.scam_name: Selçuk Old Town Carpet Shop 'Basement' Pressure Sale

stacked.headline: The Selçuk Old Town basement rug sale you 'fight your way out of'.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Selçuk Old Town basement carpet scam: 3 hours of apple tea, doors closed
stacked.pin_description: On Atatürk Caddesi in Selçuk Old Town, hotel owners and 'guides' invite you to 'see traditional weaving' at a cousin's shop. Three hours later, after apple tea, salesmen have rolled out €5,000-€30,000 rugs in a basement showroom and the doors are closed. Decline ALL invitations from hotels, drivers, and guides. From the Tabiji Turkey Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of a Selçuk Old Town basement rug pressure sale: a hotel owner offers a tourist couple to 'see my cousin's weaving', they are led down stairs into a basement showroom on Atatürk Caddesi, salesmen flip €15,000 rugs while blocking the door, and the takeaway shows the couple saying loudly 'I am not buying — please open the door.'

hook.hook: 'Come see my cousin's weaving — just 30 minutes.'
hook.pin_title: Selçuk 'come see my cousin's weaving' is the basement carpet trap
hook.pin_description: In Selçuk Old Town, any hotel owner, taxi driver, or guide who offers to take you to 'my cousin's carpet shop' or 'traditional weaving' is delivering you to a basement showroom on Atatürk Caddesi. Three hours, free apple tea, blocked doors, €5,000+ rugs. From Tabiji's Turkey scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a hotel owner in Selçuk Old Town with a friendly smile inviting a tourist couple to visit his cousin's traditional weaving shop on Atatürk Caddesi.

lesson.lesson: Never enter a shop's basement or back room.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Selçuk rule: never enter a shop's basement or back room
lesson.pin_description: The basement variant is the aggressive one — exit requires the salesman's permission. If pressured, say loudly 'I am not buying — please open the door' and walk to the entrance. For real rugs, research vetted Turkish Carpet Trade Association dealers before your trip and lock cards in the hotel safe. More Selçuk scams from Tabiji.

scams.scam_name: Pamukkale North Gate Ticket Booth Bundling Scam

stacked.headline: The Pamukkale north-gate cashier who refuses the €30 ticket and forces a €75 bundle.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Pamukkale north gate scam: cashier refuses €30 ticket, pushes €75 'mandatory' bundle
stacked.pin_description: At the Pamukkale north gate, the cashier refuses to sell the basic ₺1,200 (~€30) ticket and insists on a €60-€75 'combo package' bundling the Antique Pool, Laodicea, and audio guide as 'mandatory'. None of it is. Book in advance via muze.gov.tr to bypass the booth entirely. From the Tabiji Turkey Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Pamukkale north gate ticket-booth bundling scam: a couple asks for two basic tickets at €30, the cashier refuses and points to a €75 combo bundle calling the audio guide and Antique Pool 'mandatory', the credit-card terminal shows the higher charge, and the takeaway shows muze.gov.tr pre-bought tickets at ₺1,200.

hook.hook: 'The Antique Pool is mandatory today.' It is not.
hook.pin_title: Pamukkale 'mandatory Antique Pool entry' is invented at the gate booth
hook.pin_description: At Pamukkale's north gate, claims that the audio guide or Cleopatra Antique Pool entry is 'mandatory' or 'closed today' are invented to upsell a €60-€75 bundle on the ₺1,200 (~€30) basic ticket. Both add-ons are optional. Book on muze.gov.tr ahead. From Tabiji's Turkey scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Pamukkale north-gate cashier behind glass refusing to sell a €30 basic ticket to a couple and pointing to a €75 combo package poster claiming the Antique Pool is mandatory.

lesson.pin_description: Holding a digital ₺1,200 (~€30) Müze app ticket from muze.gov.tr removes the cashier's leverage entirely. If you must buy at the gate, photograph the credit-card terminal screen before approving and try the south gate if pushed into a bundle. Report the cashier to Pamukkale Tourism Office +90 258 272 2077. More Pamukkale scams from Tabiji.

scams.scam_name: Pamukkale Day-Trip Tour Bundled Shopping Stops

stacked.headline: The €25 Antalya day-trip with three forced shopping stops and 90 min at the travertines.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Pamukkale €25 day-trip scam: 3 shopping stops and 90 min at the travertines
stacked.pin_description: €25-€60 'all-inclusive' Pamukkale day trips from Antalya, Marmaris, or Bodrum compress the travertine visit to 90 minutes and pad the day with 2-3 'cooperative' stops — onyx jewelry, leather show, textile cooperative — each a commission point. Avoid tours under €30/person. Overnight in the village instead. From the Tabiji Turkey Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of a Pamukkale day-trip bundle from Antalya: tourists board a €25 bus at 6 AM, the itinerary shows 90 min at the travertines, the bus parks at an onyx jewelry workshop and a leather show 'demonstration', and the takeaway points to overnighting in Pamukkale village for sunrise visits at €30-€60/night.

hook.hook: '€25 all-inclusive Pamukkale day trip' — three shopping stops included.
hook.pin_title: Pamukkale €25 all-inclusive day trip math: 2-3 forced shopping stops
hook.pin_description: Any Pamukkale day-trip from Antalya, Marmaris, or Bodrum priced under €30/person funds itself through 2-3 'cooperative' stops — onyx, leather, textiles. The white travertines get 90 min; the shops get the rest of the 16-hour day. From Tabiji's Turkey scam guide.

lesson.lesson: Overnight in the village — sunrise travertines, no crowds.

lesson.pin_title: Pamukkale rule: overnight in the village for sunrise travertines
lesson.pin_description: Pamukkale village hotels run €30-€60/night and the travertines are empty before 9 AM and after 5 PM. From Antalya, hire a private driver via Welcome Pickups for €150-€250 round-trip and skip the bundle stops. For tour groups, demand 'no shopping stops' in writing or pay €40-€80 small-group rates. More Pamukkale scams from Tabiji.

scams.scam_name: Pamukkale Audio Guide & Headphone Rental Trick

stacked.headline: The Pamukkale '€5 audio guide' that becomes €25 on return.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Turkey Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Pamukkale audio-guide scam: '€5' verbal becomes €25 on return
stacked.pin_description: At the Pamukkale gate audio-guide kiosk, the clerk says headphones are €5 and you walk in. On return, the bill is €25 — '€5 was per hour' or 'the audio was €20 extra'. Some demand a €40 deposit they refuse to refund citing imaginary damage. Decline rentals; use GPSmyCity Pamukkale (€3.99). From the Tabiji Turkey Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Pamukkale audio-guide bait-and-switch: a clerk at the gate kiosk hands a tourist headphones quoting '€5', a tourist walks the travertines listening, on return the kiosk demands €25 citing 'per hour' fine print, and the takeaway points to the GPSmyCity app at €3.99 one-time.

hook.hook: 'Audio guide €5' verbal — that bill comes back at €25.
hook.pin_title: Pamukkale '€5 audio guide' verbal turns into €25 on return
hook.pin_description: If the Pamukkale audio-guide clerk only quotes '€5' verbally with no printed receipt, the price is intentionally ambiguous — per hour, per device, per person? On return the bill jumps to €25, or a €40 'deposit' is withheld for imagined damage. Get the full price in writing first. From Tabiji's Turkey scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Pamukkale audio-guide kiosk clerk handing headphones to a tourist while saying just '€5' with no printed receipt or terms displayed.

lesson.lesson: Skip the gate kiosk — use GPSmyCity for €3.99.

lesson.pin_title: Pamukkale rule: skip the gate kiosk, use GPSmyCity for €3.99
lesson.pin_description: Pamukkale is small and well-signposted — a downloaded Wikipedia article or the GPSmyCity Pamukkale app (€3.99 one-time) is enough. If you do rent at the kiosk, photograph the device condition at pickup, get the full price in writing, and refuse 'deposit' demands over €10. More Pamukkale scams from Tabiji.

stacked.pin_description: At the Cleopatra Antique Pool inside Pamukkale, cashiers quote €15-€20 for entry that officially costs ₺240 (~€6). Locker rental quoted €5 bills at €10-€15 'per item'; a 'mandatory special towel' adds €8; pool photographers' '€5 photo' becomes €25 once printed. Bring your own towel and lock-bag. From the Tabiji Turkey Scam Survival Guide.

hook.pin_description: The Cleopatra Antique Pool inside Pamukkale charges ₺240 (~€6) at the posted board for entry — refuse any quote above ₺300. The pool entry is one transaction; locker, towel, and photographer upsells are all optional add-ons priced as 'mandatory'. From Tabiji's Turkey scam guide.

Decline poolside photographers — the official Pamukkale visitor app provides location-tagged photos free. Visit 8-10 AM before the day-trippers arrive after 11. More Pamukkale scams from Tabiji.

scams.scam_name: Hot Air Balloon Operator Pricing & Safety Variance

stacked.headline: The €60 Pamukkale 'cruise-day balloon' flown unlicensed without DGCA SHGM clearance.

stacked.pin_description: Below €100 per person, a parallel ring sells 'special €60 Pamukkale balloon flights' that may run 15-20 min instead of the advertised 60-75, cancel at the launch field with no refund, or fly without Turkish DGCA SHGM licensing. Book Pamukkale Balloons, Sky Pamukkale, or Royal Balloon at €120-€180. From the Tabiji Turkey Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: 'Special €60 cruise-day balloon flight.' That price funds skipped maintenance.
hook.pin_title: Pamukkale '€60 special balloon flight' is the unlicensed-operator price
hook.pin_description: Legitimate Pamukkale balloon operators (Pamukkale Balloons, Sky Pamukkale, Royal Balloon) charge €120-€180 per person for a 60-75 min sunrise flight with breakfast and certificate. Anything under €100 signals an unlicensed operator skipping Turkish DGCA SHGM safety compliance. From Tabiji's Turkey scam guide.

lesson.pin_description: Book directly with Pamukkale Balloons (pamukkaleballoons.com), Sky Pamukkale, or Royal Balloon and ask for their Turkish DGCA SHGM licensing number. hook.pin_description: Turkish KDV (VAT) at 10-20% is legally required to be INCLUDED in menu prices — any Konya restaurant adding 'KDV' as a separate line on the bill is operating illegally. Refuse and ask for the bill recalculated. From Tabiji's Turkey scam guide.

stacked.pin_description: In Goreme, scammers run clone websites of legit balloon companies, take $200 deposits via card, and disappear. The 4 AM launch-day shuttle never arrives, the phone is disconnected, the email bounces. Book directly with Butterfly Balloons, Royal Balloon, or Voyager Balloons — verify the URL exactly, never pay by bank transfer. From the Tabiji Turkey Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: "Apple tea — no obligation, just hospitality."
hook.pin_title: Goreme carpet rule: apple-tea hospitality is the 200 EUR sales technique
hook.pin_description: On Goreme main street, any 'no obligation, just hospitality' apple-tea invitation at a carpet shop is the opening of an hour-long sales session. The 'silk' carpet that drops from 5,000 to 2,000 EUR is machine-made and worth 35 EUR on Amazon. Tea is fine — buying isn't required. From Tabiji's Turkey scam guide.

stacked.pin_description: Days before a Goreme cave hotel stay, a WhatsApp message from an unfamiliar number claims your Booking.com reservation was lost to 'internet issues' and asks you to pay again via a new link — a phishing page. Alternatively, on arrival, the hotel says the Booking.com price was 'wrong' and demands cash at a higher rate, threatening to give your room away. From the Tabiji Turkey Scam Survival Guide.

hook.pin_description: Any WhatsApp or SMS message about your Goreme cave hotel booking from a number not listed on the hotel website, asking you to 'pay again' via a link, is phishing. Contact the hotel directly using the Booking.com number. Screenshot your confirmation with the price and show it at check-in. From Tabiji's Turkey scam guide.

Screenshot your booking confirmation with the price and show it at check-in. If staff demand cash at a higher rate, contact Booking.com support from the lobby. stacked.pin_description: Inside Beijing Capital (PEK) and Daxing (PKX) arrivals, touts pitch "Taxi? Fixed price, no meter" and quote ¥400-¥800 to the city — three to five times the metered ¥90-¥120 (PEK) or ¥140-¥180 (PKX). Take the Airport Express (¥25, 25 min from PEK) or say 'da biao' at the official rank. From the Tabiji Beijing Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: "Taxi? Fixed price, no meter!" Walk to the rank.

hook.pin_description: Anyone inside Beijing PEK or Daxing PKX arrivals saying "Taxi? Fixed price, no meter" is unauthorized and will charge ¥400-¥800 for a ¥90-¥180 metered ride. Follow the 'Taxi' signs to the outdoor rank, say 'da biao' (打表) before the car moves. From Tabiji's Beijing scam guide.

lesson.pin_description: PEK to central Beijing is ¥90-¥120 metered, ¥25 on the Airport Express (25 min). Daxing PKX is ¥140-¥180 metered, ¥35 on the Daxing Express metro. Photograph the plate as you board. Never engage a driver inside the terminal. More Beijing scams from Tabiji.

hook.hook: "I am official guide — 200 yuan per hour." Walk to the audio rental.

hook.pin_description: Anyone in a vest at the Temple of Heaven, Summer Palace, or Lama Temple gate saying "I am official guide — 200 yuan per hour" is unlicensed and will demand ¥800 in twenty minutes. Real guides are booked in advance via the ticket office or Viator. From Tabiji's Beijing scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a man in a homemade laminated 'guide' vest at the Beijing Temple of Heaven main gate approaching a tourist with '¥200 per hour, I show you everything.'

lesson.lesson: Rent the official audio guide at the gate.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Beijing park rule: rent the official audio guide at the gate
lesson.pin_description: Official audio guides are ¥40 at the Temple of Heaven, ¥60 at the Summer Palace, ¥40 at the Forbidden City. Book guided tours in advance via Viator or GetYourGuide; never accept gate-approach guides. If a tout has attached himself, refuse to pay and threaten to call 110. More Beijing scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at the Beijing Temple of Heaven entrance holding the ¥40 official audio-guide rental device, with the takeaway 'Rent the official audio guide at the gate.'

scams.scam_name: Tianfu Airport (TFU) & Chengdu Shuangliu (CTU) Taxi Scams
scams.location: Tianfu International Airport (TFU) arrivals, Chengdu Shuangliu International Airport (CTU), airport-to-panda-base transfers

stacked.headline: The Chengdu TFU tout charging ¥800 for a ¥200 metered ride.
stacked.brand_sub: From the China Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Chengdu TFU & CTU taxi scam: "fixed price" ¥500-¥800 for a ¥80-¥220 ride
stacked.pin_description: Touts inside Tianfu (TFU) and Shuangliu (CTU) arrivals quote ¥500-¥800 fixed when the meter would run ¥180-¥220 from TFU or ¥80-¥110 from CTU. Take Metro Line 18 from TFU (¥9, 47 min) or Metro Line 10 from CTU (¥6, 25 min) instead. From the Tabiji Chengdu Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Chengdu Tianfu airport taxi scam: a man waves at a tourist inside TFU arrivals offering 'taxi, fixed price', the driver loads bags quoting ¥800 to Chunxi Road, the meter is bypassed all the way into central Chengdu, and the takeaway points to Metro Line 18 at ¥9.

hook.hook: "Taxi, fixed price ¥600!" Walk to the metro.
hook.pin_title: Chengdu TFU "taxi, fixed price ¥600" is the unlicensed tout pitch
hook.pin_description: Anyone waving inside Chengdu TFU or Shuangliu CTU arrivals saying "taxi, fixed price" is unauthorized — the meter from TFU is ¥180-¥220 and from CTU ¥80-¥110. Metro Line 18 from TFU is ¥9, Line 10 from CTU is ¥6. Say 'da biao' (打表) at the rank if you take a cab. From Tabiji's Chengdu scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a man inside Chengdu Tianfu Airport arrivals waving at a tourist with luggage offering 'taxi, fixed price ¥600' to Chunxi Road.

lesson.lesson: Take Metro Line 18 from TFU.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Chengdu airport rule: take Metro Line 18 from TFU
lesson.pin_description: Metro Line 18 from TFU to Tianfu Square is ¥9 in 47 minutes. Metro Line 10 from CTU to Taipingyuan is ¥6 in 25 minutes. DiDi at the official rideshare zone is ~¥150-¥200 from TFU. Photograph the plate and report overcharges to 12315 or 110. More Chengdu scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at the Chengdu Tianfu Airport Metro Line 18 platform holding a ¥9 ticket to Tianfu Square, with the takeaway 'Take Metro Line 18 from TFU.'

scams.scam_name: Chengdu Tibet Tour Permit & Package Scam
scams.location: Chengdu hotels, Chengdu North Railway Station booths, online travel sites marketing 'Chengdu + Tibet' packages

stacked.headline: The Chengdu ¥600 'Tibet permit' tour that strands you in Lhasa.
stacked.brand_sub: From the China Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Chengdu Tibet permit scam: ¥600-¥3,000 tours when the legitimate floor is ¥6,000
stacked.pin_description: 'Chengdu + Tibet' operators pitch Tibet Travel Permit packages at ¥600-¥3,000 when the legitimate floor is ¥6,000+. Outcomes: outright fraud, bait-and-switch shopping stops, or paid Everest Base Camp downgraded to a 3-day Lhasa loop. Book only Tibet Vista, Explore Tibet, or Great Tibet Tour and pay by card. From the Tabiji Chengdu Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Chengdu Tibet permit scam: a hotel booth offers a 'Chengdu + Tibet' package at ¥600 per person, the operator demands cash and refuses to name the permit number, the tourist arrives in Lhasa with no permit and no recourse, and the takeaway points to Tibet Vista as the licensed credit-card-accepting alternative.

hook.hook: "Chengdu + Tibet package, only ¥600 — bank transfer please." Refuse.
hook.pin_title: Chengdu "Tibet package ¥600 — bank transfer please" never gets a permit
hook.pin_description: If a Chengdu hotel or North Railway Station booth offers a Tibet permit package at ¥600-¥3,000 and demands bank transfer or cash with no credit card, the permit number will not exist and you'll be stranded. The legitimate floor is ¥6,000+ via Tibet Vista or Explore Tibet. From Tabiji's Chengdu scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Chengdu hotel-lobby travel agent offering a glossy 'Chengdu + Tibet ¥600 per person' brochure to a tourist.

lesson.lesson: Verify the permit number. Pay by credit card.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Chengdu Tibet rule: verify the permit number, pay by credit card
lesson.pin_description: Book Tibet only with permit-licensed operators (Tibet Vista, Explore Tibet, Great Tibet Tour, Budget Tibet Tour) and verify the permit number on the Tibet Tourism Bureau site before flying to Lhasa. Pay by credit card; expect ¥6,000-¥12,000 for 4-8 days. Reject anything under ¥3,000. More Chengdu scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at home checking a Tibet Travel Permit number on the Tibet Tourism Bureau website before booking a flight, with the takeaway 'Verify the permit number. Pay by credit card.'

scams.scam_name: Chengdu Panda Base Tour Package Overcharge
scams.location: Chengdu Research Base of Giant Panda Breeding, Dujiangyan Panda Base, Wolong Panda Base, hotel-concierge tour packages

stacked.headline: The Chengdu ¥400 'VIP panda tour' for what costs ¥90 alone.
stacked.brand_sub: From the China Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Chengdu Panda Base scam: ¥300-¥500 'VIP tours' for a ¥90 independent trip
stacked.pin_description: Hotel concierges sell Panda Base 'VIP tours' at ¥300-¥500 when independent cost is ¥90 (¥55 entry + ¥35 metro/shuttle). The promised 'photo with panda' is not available to adult foreign tourists. Book entry on the official WeChat mini-program and ride Metro Line 3 to Panda Avenue. From the Tabiji Chengdu Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: "Panda VIP tour with photo opportunity, ¥400!" Decline.
hook.pin_title: Chengdu "Panda VIP tour with photo opportunity ¥400" is a ¥90 trip oversold
hook.pin_description: If a Chengdu hotel concierge or entrance tout sells a 'Panda Base VIP tour with photo opportunity' at ¥300-¥500, the photo program is not available to adult foreign tourists and the entire trip costs ¥90 independently (¥55 entry + ¥35 transport). From Tabiji's Chengdu scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Chengdu hotel concierge handing a tourist a ¥400 'Panda VIP Tour with Photo Opportunity' brochure at the front desk.

lesson.lesson: Book the ¥55 entry on the official WeChat.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Chengdu panda rule: book the ¥55 entry on the official WeChat
lesson.pin_description: Book Panda Base entry (¥55 adult) via the WeChat mini-program 成都大熊猫繁育研究基地 or Trip.com. Take Metro Line 3 to Panda Avenue Station (¥4) plus shuttle #16. Arrive before 8:30 AM for active feeding. For a guide, use Viator (¥200-¥300, no shopping stops). More Chengdu scams from Tabiji.

scams.scam_name: Chengdu Tea House Scam at Kuanzhai Alley & Jinli
scams.location: Kuanzhai Xiangzi (Wide and Narrow Alley) tourist strip, Jinli Ancient Street, People's Park tea-garden entrances

stacked.headline: The Chengdu 'Sichuan tea ceremony' billing ¥2,500 for ¥30 worth of tea.
stacked.brand_sub: From the China Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Chengdu Kuanzhai & Jinli tea scam: ¥800-¥2,500 bills, 10-20× residential rate
stacked.pin_description: Fluent-English strangers at Kuanzhai Alley, Jinli Street, and People's Park invite tourists to a 'traditional Sichuan tea ceremony' on a side street. Bills land at ¥800-¥2,500 per person — 10-20× the ¥15-¥40 residential pot rate. Go to People's Park Heming Tea Garden (¥15-¥30) instead. From the Tabiji Chengdu Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Chengdu Kuanzhai Alley tea-house scam: a fluent-English stranger asks 'where are you from?', invites a tourist to a 'traditional Sichuan tea ceremony' upstairs on a side lane, the bill arrives at ¥2,500 with no menu shown, and the takeaway points to People's Park Heming Tea Garden at ¥20 per pot.

hook.hook: "Try a traditional Sichuan tea ceremony nearby?" Walk past.
hook.pin_title: Chengdu "traditional Sichuan tea ceremony nearby" lands a ¥2,500 bill
hook.pin_description: If a fluent-English stranger at Kuanzhai Alley, Jinli, or People's Park invites you to a 'traditional Sichuan tea ceremony' at a side-street venue, the bill will land at ¥800-¥2,500 per person — 10-20× the residential ¥15-¥40 pot rate. Reply 'bu yao, xie xie'. From Tabiji's Chengdu scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a fluent-English stranger at Kuanzhai Alley in Chengdu approaching a tourist with 'where are you from? Want to try a traditional Sichuan tea ceremony nearby?'

lesson.lesson: Go straight to People's Park Heming Tea Garden.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Chengdu tea rule: go straight to People's Park Heming Tea Garden
lesson.pin_description: For real Sichuan tea, go to People's Park Heming Tea Garden (Renmin Park west entrance, ¥15-¥30 per pot, bottomless refills) or Wenshu Monastery tea garden (¥20-¥40). Both have posted prices and serve locals. Never follow a stranger to a side-street tea house. Pay by card if trapped. More Chengdu scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist seated at People's Park Heming Tea Garden in Chengdu with a ¥20 pot of green tea and bamboo chairs, with the takeaway 'Go straight to People's Park Heming Tea Garden.'

scams.location: Kuanzhai Alley hotpot rows, Jinli Ancient Street hotpot venues, tourist-facing Haolaihui and near Tianfu Square

stacked.headline: The Chengdu tourist hotpot billing ¥500 for a ¥130 dinner.
stacked.brand_sub: From the China Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Chengdu hotpot tourist scam: ¥300-¥500 menus on Kuanzhai vs ¥90-¥170 a street away
stacked.pin_description: Laminated-English-menu hotpot on Kuanzhai Alley, Jinli, and near Tianfu Square charges ¥300-¥500 per person — double-to-triple Shu Jiu Xiang or Huang Cheng Lao Ma at ¥90-¥170. 'Premium' side plates run ¥80, 'spicy fees' tack on. Walk one street off and book Dianping. From the Tabiji Chengdu Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Chengdu hotpot tourist-menu scam: a tout outside a Kuanzhai Alley restaurant calls 'famous hotpot' in English, the laminated photo menu shows ¥80 'premium' side plates, the bill lands at ¥500 with a 'spicy fee' added, and the takeaway points to Shu Jiu Xiang one street off at ¥120 per person.

hook.hook: "Famous hotpot, English menu!" Walk one street off.
hook.pin_title: Chengdu "famous hotpot, English menu" is double-to-triple a Dianping venue
hook.pin_description: If a tout on Kuanzhai Alley or Jinli calls 'famous hotpot' in English with a laminated photo menu, the bill will land at ¥300-¥500 per person — versus ¥90-¥170 at Shu Jiu Xiang, Huang Cheng Lao Ma, or Da Long Yi one street off. Book via Dianping; 4.5-star is reliable. From Tabiji's Chengdu scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a hotpot tout on Kuanzhai Alley in Chengdu waving a laminated English-photo menu calling 'famous hotpot' to a tourist couple.

lesson.lesson: Book Shu Jiu Xiang on Dianping.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Chengdu hotpot rule: book Shu Jiu Xiang on Dianping
lesson.pin_description: Authentic Chengdu hotpot runs ¥90-¥170 per person at Shu Jiu Xiang (¥90-¥130), Huang Cheng Lao Ma (¥120-¥180), Da Long Yi (¥130-¥170), or Xiao Long Kan (¥100-¥140). Book via Dianping; 4.5+ stars is reliable. Order yuanyang broth, say 'yi dian dian la' if heat is new. More Chengdu scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at Shu Jiu Xiang in Chengdu booked via Dianping with a yuanyang half-spicy half-mild hotpot at ¥120 per person, with the takeaway 'Book Shu Jiu Xiang on Dianping.'

scams.scam_name: Chengdu Jade, TCM & Silk 'Museum' Shopping Tours
scams.location: Tour bus stops along panda-base, Dujiangyan, Mount Emei, and Jiuzhaigou day-trip routes from Chengdu; hotel-concierge 'cultural tour' packages

stacked.headline: The Chengdu cultural tour where 4 of the stops are jade shops.
stacked.brand_sub: From the China Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Chengdu jade & TCM 'museum' tour scam: 4 shopping stops in 2 days, 20% delivered
stacked.pin_description: 'Chengdu cultural tour' packages to Mount Emei, Leshan, Dujiangyan, and Jiuzhaigou bundle 4-6 forced 45-minute jade, TCM, silk, and tea 'museum' stops — one community report logged 4 scam stops across 2 days with 20% of the itinerary delivered. Demand zero shopping in writing or self-guide via high-speed rail. From the Tabiji Chengdu Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Chengdu jade and TCM museum shopping tour: a hotel concierge pushes a 'government certified cultural tour' to Mount Emei, the bus pulls into a jade museum on the way, the tourist sits through a 45-minute commission sales pitch, and the takeaway shows a Chengdu high-speed rail ticket to Mount Emei at ¥65.

hook.hook: "Government-certified cultural tour, jade museum included." Skip it.
hook.pin_title: Chengdu "government-certified cultural tour" is 4-6 forced shopping stops
hook.pin_description: If a Chengdu hotel concierge pitches a 'government-certified cultural tour' to Mount Emei, Leshan, or Jiuzhaigou under ¥200 per day or under ¥1,500 for Jiuzhaigou multi-day, the trip is 30%+ jade, TCM, silk, and tea 'museum' stops. Demand zero shopping in writing. From Tabiji's Chengdu scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Chengdu hotel concierge handing a tourist a 'Government-Certified Cultural Tour Mount Emei ¥180' brochure at the front desk.

lesson.lesson: Self-guide via high-speed rail.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Chengdu tour rule: self-guide via high-speed rail
lesson.pin_description: Chengdu's high-speed rail puts Mount Emei (1.5 hrs, ¥65), Leshan (1 hr, ¥55), and Dujiangyan (30 min, ¥15) within self-guided range. For Jiuzhaigou, fly direct to Jiuzhaigou Huanglong Airport. Licensed Viator tours run ¥300-¥800 per day with zero shopping in writing. File 12315 for chargebacks. More Chengdu scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at the Chengdu East high-speed rail station holding a ¥65 ticket to Mount Emei, with the takeaway 'Self-guide via high-speed rail.'

scams.scam_name: Jinli Ancient Street & Kuanzhai Alley Souvenir Overcharge
scams.location: Jinli Ancient Street (inside Wuhou Shrine area), Kuanzhai Xiangzi (Wide and Narrow Alley), People's Park handicraft vendors

stacked.headline: The Jinli bian lian mask priced ¥200 — sold for ¥30 a metro stop away.
stacked.brand_sub: From the China Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Chengdu Jinli & Kuanzhai souvenir scam: bian lian masks ¥80-¥200 vs ¥20-¥50
stacked.pin_description: Jinli Ancient Street and Kuanzhai Alley sell Sichuan opera bian lian masks at ¥80-¥200, silk scrolls at ¥150-¥400, and Shu embroidery at ¥200-¥800 — 2-5× the rates at Tongji Road or the Qingyang Taoist Temple Sunday market. Decline 'free tea tasting' setups. From the Tabiji Chengdu Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Jinli Ancient Street souvenir overcharge: a Kuanzhai Alley stall offers a 'free tea tasting' to a tourist, the merchant displays bian lian masks priced at ¥200, the tourist hesitates as he pours another cup of tea, and the takeaway points to the Qingyang Taoist Temple Sunday market with masks at ¥30.

hook.hook: "Free tea tasting — handmade bian lian for ¥200." Decline.
hook.pin_title: Chengdu "free tea tasting, handmade bian lian ¥200" is a 5x overcharge
hook.pin_description: If a Jinli or Kuanzhai stall offers 'free tea tasting' and shows handmade bian lian masks at ¥80-¥200, the same masks are ¥20-¥50 at Tongji Road and ¥20-¥60 at the Qingyang Taoist Temple Sunday market. The free tea is the pressure setup. Walk away. From Tabiji's Chengdu scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Jinli Ancient Street stall vendor in Chengdu pouring free tea while displaying a ¥200 Sichuan opera bian lian mask to a tourist.

lesson.lesson: Shop Tongji Road, not Jinli.

lesson.pin_title: Chengdu souvenir rule: shop Tongji Road, not Jinli
lesson.pin_description: For Sichuan souvenirs, go to Tongji Road Souvenir Market (2-3× cheaper), the Qingyang Taoist Temple Sunday market for ¥20-¥60 bian lian masks, the Shu Brocade and Embroidery Museum gift shop, or Wenshu Monastery stalls. If shopping Jinli for convenience, start negotiations at 30% of first quote. More Chengdu scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at the Qingyang Taoist Temple Sunday market in Chengdu holding a ¥30 bian lian mask, with the takeaway 'Shop Tongji Road, not Jinli.'

scams.location: Guilin hotel lobbies, Magu Pier, Zhujiang Pier booking booths, Yangshuo arrival docks

stacked.pin_title: Li River cruise scam: Guilin hotel lobby quotes ¥500-¥800 for a ¥215 ticket
stacked.pin_description: Guilin hotel-lobby booths quote ¥500-¥800 for the standard 4-hour Li River cruise to Yangshuo. The real Magu Pier ticket is ¥215 tourist class, ¥310 deluxe via Trip.com, Viator, or Ctrip. Avoid 'all-in-one Guilin + Yangshuo' tours under ¥600 — guaranteed jade museum, silk factory, and tea ceremony shopping stops. From the Tabiji Guilin Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: "Li River cruise package, ¥800 with hotel pickup." Walk past.
hook.foot: Guilin Li River cruise scam  ·  tabiji.ai
hook.pin_title: Guilin hotel "Li River cruise package ¥800" is a ¥215 ticket plus markup
hook.pin_description: Any Guilin hotel-lobby booth pitching a ¥500-¥800 'Li River cruise package' is selling a ¥215 Magu Pier ticket plus 2-3x commission. Book the standard 4-hour cruise on Trip.com, Viator, or Ctrip and the Magu transfer bus separately at ¥50-¥80. From Tabiji's Guilin scam guide.

lesson.lesson: Book Magu Pier direct, never the lobby.

Pre-arrange the ¥50-¥80 Magu transfer bus and the Yangshuo hotel pickup separately. Reject any 'all-in-one' package under ¥600 — the shopping stops are guaranteed. More Guilin scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist couple at Magu Pier holding their phone open to a Trip.com ¥215 Li River cruise booking, with the takeaway 'Book Magu Pier direct, never the lobby.'

stacked.pin_description: Touts on West Street offer Yangshuo bamboo rafts at ¥80 — what arrives is a 30-minute float in a stagnant backwater, not the 90-minute Yulong River route. The fair rate is ¥150-¥200 per 2-person raft booked through your guesthouse. The 'cormorant fishing show' is staged with chained birds, and the photo fisherman on the Li River wants ¥20-¥50 per shot. From the Tabiji Guilin Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: "Discount bamboo raft, ¥80 only!" Refuse.
hook.pin_title: Yangshuo West Street "discount raft ¥80" is a 30-min backwater swap
hook.pin_description: Anyone on Yangshuo's West Street pitching a ¥80 bamboo raft is selling a 30-minute backwater float, not the 90-minute Yulong River route that costs ¥150-¥200 per 2-person raft. Book through a guesthouse with posted prices and skip the staged cormorant shows. From Tabiji's Guilin scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Yangshuo tout on West Street in a straw hat shouting 'discount bamboo raft, ¥80!' to a tourist couple walking past.

lesson.lesson: Book through your guesthouse, not West Street.

lesson.pin_title: Yangshuo raft rule: book through your guesthouse, not West Street
lesson.pin_description: The Yulong River 90-minute bamboo raft is ¥150-¥200 per 2-person at any Yangshuo guesthouse with posted prices. Skip cormorant shows (staged, chained birds), refuse photo demands from fishermen on the Li River, and walk one block off West Street for honest food. More Guilin scams from Tabiji.

hook.hook: "Guilin city, ¥300, meter broken." Walk to the bus.
hook.pin_title: Guilin KWL "meter broken, ¥300 fixed" is the unlicensed pitch
hook.pin_description: Any KWL or Guilin Railway Station driver saying 'meter broken' or quoting a ¥200-¥300 fixed price is unlicensed — the metered fare to the city center is ¥100-¥130. Use the ¥25 Airport Shuttle Bus, DiDi at the rideshare zone, or insist on 'da biao' (打表). From Tabiji's Guilin scam guide.

lesson.lesson: Always say "da biao" or take the ¥25 bus.

lesson.pin_title: Guilin taxi rule: always say "da biao" or take the ¥25 bus

If you take a licensed taxi, say 'da biao' (打表) — the metered city-center fare is ¥100-¥130 and the KWL-to-Yangshuo airport bus is ¥50. More Guilin scams from Tabiji.

stacked.pin_description: Unlicensed booths at Luohu Commercial City, Huanggang, and Futian Checkpoint charge 3-8% above the posted rate and sometimes slip counterfeit ¥100 notes among legitimate currency. Use Bank of China, HSBC, Standard Chartered, or Wing Lung licensed money-changers — visible branded signs and posted rates. Or use Wise/Revolut at a Bank of China ATM (~1% margin). From the Tabiji Shenzhen Scam Survival Guide.

hook.pin_description: Any unlicensed booth at Luohu Commercial City, Huanggang, or Futian Checkpoint offering a "better rate than the bank" charges 3-8% over the posted rate and may slip counterfeit ¥100 notes into the stack. Use Bank of China, HSBC, Standard Chartered, or Wing Lung. From Tabiji's Shenzhen scam guide.

stacked.headline: The Guangzhou ¥50,000 "contract celebration" hostess-bar bill.

stacked.pin_title: Canton Fair hostess-bar scam: ¥10,000-¥50,000 bill at supplier-chosen venue
stacked.pin_description: During Canton Fair (April-May, October-November) and year-round in Zhujiang New Town, "suppliers" invite buyers to hostess bars or private rooms where ¥800-¥2,000 per drink leads to ¥10,000-¥50,000 bills. Insist on a hotel restaurant or Dianping-verified 4.5+ venue. Pay with credit card. If trapped, refuse excess and call 110. From the Tabiji Guangzhou Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: "Let me pick the contract dinner venue." Refuse.
hook.pin_title: Guangzhou "contract celebration dinner" = ¥10,000+ hostess-bar bill
hook.pin_description: If a Canton Fair contact insists on choosing a venue near Pazhou or Zhujiang New Town with no English menu and ¥500+ drinks, it's a hostess-bar scam — bills run ¥10,000-¥50,000. Eat at Lin Heung Tea House, Tao Heung, or Panxi Restaurant in Liwan Park instead. From Tabiji's Guangzhou scam guide.

hook.hook: "Private car direct to Pingyao, ¥400." The train is ¥23.

scams.scam_name: Harbin Ice and Snow Festival Ticket & 'Snow Village' Overcharge
scams.location: Harbin Ice and Snow World (Songhua River island), Zhongyang Street tourist strip, 'Snow Village' (Xuexiang) day trip destinations

stacked.headline: The Harbin Ice and Snow World "VIP" at ¥1,200 vs ¥460 evening official.

stacked.pin_title: Harbin Ice and Snow World scam: "VIP" ¥800-¥1,200 vs ¥330 day / ¥460 evening

Third-party WeChat resellers push 'VIP' at ¥800-¥1,200 — no official VIP exists. Skip Snow Village (Xuexiang) packages at ¥600-¥1,500. From the Tabiji Harbin Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of a Harbin Ice and Snow World festival ticket scam: a WeChat reseller offers a 'VIP package ¥1,000', the tourist sees Trip.com posting ¥460 evening official, she rebooks direct, and the takeaway points to skipping the 'Snow Village 2-day' add-on for Volga Manor or Siberian Tiger Park.

hook.hook: "Ice and Snow World VIP, ¥1,000 each." No VIP exists.
hook.pin_title: Harbin Ice and Snow World "VIP" reseller is just ¥460 evening at 2-3x
hook.pin_description: If a Harbin WeChat or Facebook reseller pitches an Ice and Snow World 'VIP' at ¥800-¥1,200, no official VIP exists — book direct on Ctrip / Trip.com at ¥330 day / ¥460 evening. Skip Snow Village 'overnight' bundles at ¥1,500+. From Tabiji's Harbin scam guide.

scams.scam_name: Harbin Airport (HRB) & Winter Transit Taxi Overcharge
scams.location: Harbin Taiping International Airport (HRB) arrivals, Harbin Railway Station, Harbin West Railway Station (HSR), winter conditions adding confusion

stacked.headline: The Harbin "snow surcharge ¥100" — there is no official snow surcharge.
stacked.brand_sub: From the China Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Harbin HRB airport taxi scam: "snow surcharge" ¥100-¥350 fake; metered fare ¥110-¥150
stacked.pin_description: At Harbin Taiping International Airport (HRB), legitimate metered taxi to central Harbin is ¥110-¥150 (winter weather can legitimately add 10-30%). Touts inside arrivals quote ¥300-¥500 'fixed price' or add a ¥100 'snow surcharge' on the meter. There is no official snow surcharge in Harbin. Take Airport Shuttle Bus Line 1 to Zhongyang Street: ¥20, 45 min, heated. From the Tabiji Harbin Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of a Harbin HRB airport winter taxi scam: a driver inside arrivals offers '¥350 fixed price winter taxi', the meter runs and the driver adds '¥100 snow supplement' at destination, the tourist refuses citing no official surcharge, and the takeaway points to Airport Shuttle Bus Line 1 to Zhongyang Street at ¥20.

hook.hook: "Winter surcharge, ¥350 fixed." Walk to the shuttle bus.
hook.pin_title: Harbin HRB "winter surcharge ¥350 fixed" — there is no official surcharge
hook.pin_description: If an HRB driver quotes ¥300-¥500 'fixed' or adds a ¥100 'snow supplement' on the meter, no official Harbin snow surcharge exists. Real metered fare is ¥110-¥180 winter; Airport Shuttle Bus Line 1 to Zhongyang Street is ¥20, 45 min, heated. From Tabiji's Harbin scam guide.

lesson.pin_description: From Harbin Taiping (HRB), Shuttle Bus Line 1 runs to Zhongyang Street at ¥20 in 45 min and Line 2 to Harbin Railway Station at ¥20 in 50 min — both heated through winter. If you must take a taxi, 'da biao' for ¥110-¥180 to center and reject any 'snow surcharge'. More Harbin scams from Tabiji.

scams.location: Zhongyang Street (Central Street) pedestrian shopping strip, Russian-themed souvenir shops, 'Russian fur coat' retailers, Modern Hotel area

stacked.headline: The Harbin "Russian mink" at ¥15,000 — often dyed rabbit.
stacked.brand_sub: From the China Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Harbin Zhongyang Street souvenir scam: "Russian mink" ¥2,000-¥15,000 often dyed rabbit
stacked.pin_description: On Zhongyang Street, 'authentic Russian matryoshka' at ¥300-¥800 is Zhejiang factory-made (¥30-¥100 at supermarkets), 'Russian mink' coats at ¥2,000-¥15,000 are often rabbit or synthetic, and 'Russian chocolate' at ¥80 a bar is ¥15 at Chao Shi Fa or Walmart. Fur only at licensed retailers with CITES. From the Tabiji Harbin Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: "Authentic Russian mink, ¥9,000 today." Often dyed rabbit.
hook.pin_title: Harbin Zhongyang Street "Russian mink ¥9,000" is often rabbit or synthetic
hook.pin_description: On Harbin's Zhongyang Street, 'Russian mink' at ¥2,000-¥15,000 is often rabbit or synthetic dyed to look premium — buy fur only at licensed branded retailers with CITES certification. Matryoshka at ¥30-¥100 at residential department stores. From Tabiji's Harbin scam guide.

Matryoshka at residential department stores ¥30-¥100. Russian amber at Daowai Russian Tourist Market with better markups. More Harbin scams from Tabiji.

stacked.pin_description: Zhongyang Street 'Russian' restaurants charge ¥300-¥700 per person — borscht ¥80+, chicken kiev ¥200+, beef stroganoff ¥250+. Genuine Russian institutions cost ¥100-¥300: Lucia Russian Restaurant, Harbin Portman Western, Russian Russia Restaurant. Order via Dianping. Skip 'Stalin's favorite' or 'Russian grandmother's kitchen' marketing. From the Tabiji Harbin Scam Survival Guide.

hook.pin_description: If a Harbin Zhongyang Street venue markets 'Stalin's favorite recipe' or 'Russian grandmother's kitchen' with a laminated English/Russian menu, expect ¥300-¥700 per person — borscht ¥80+ (real ¥25-¥45), chicken kiev ¥200+ (real ¥80-¥120). Book Lucia or Harbin Portman via Dianping. From Tabiji's Harbin scam guide.

lesson.pin_description: Lucia Russian Restaurant (¥150-¥300), Harbin Portman Western (¥120-¥200), Russian Russia Restaurant (¥100-¥180), and Modern Hotel's Russian Bar (¥100-¥200) are the real Harbin-Russian institutions on Dianping. Order borscht, chicken kiev, gelieba, hongchang. More Harbin scams from Tabiji.

stacked.headline: The Sydney taxi 'top-up' that turns a A$48 fare into A$85.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Australia Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Sydney Airport taxi 'top-up' scam: A$48 meter becomes A$85 cash demand
stacked.pin_description: At Sydney Airport T1, drivers run the meter to ~A$48 then add a fake 'top-up' for tolls and a late-night surcharge, demanding A$85 cash at your hotel. There is no separate late-night fee — it is in the meter. Pre-book Uber, DiDi or Bolt at the rideshare bay. From the Tabiji Sydney Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Sydney Airport taxi top-up scam: a tout waves a tourist past the Uber queue at T1, the driver runs the meter to A$48 to the CBD, points at the screen demanding A$85 cash for a fake toll and late-night surcharge, and the takeaway points the tourist back to the rideshare bay.

hook.hook: "There's a top-up for tolls and the late-night rate." Refuse.
hook.pin_title: Sydney Airport "top-up for tolls and the late-night rate" is a A$37 scam
hook.pin_description: If a Sydney Airport driver says "there's a top-up for tolls and the late-night rate" after running the meter to A$48, they're inflating it to A$85 with fake fees. The late-night rate is already in the meter. Use Uber, DiDi, Bolt, 13cabs or Silver Service. From Tabiji's Sydney scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Sydney taxi driver at a CBD hotel pointing at his meter showing A$85 telling a jet-lagged tourist with luggage that there is a top-up for tolls and the late-night rate.

lesson.lesson: Tap to pay. Never hand over the card.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Sydney taxi rule: tap to pay, never hand over the card
lesson.pin_description: Insist on tap-to-pay at the in-car terminal on every Sydney taxi — the legitimate CBD fare from the airport is A$45-A$60. Drivers claiming the terminal is broken and asking you to swipe are cloning your magnetic stripe. Amex disputes succeed if you are overcharged. More Sydney scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a Sydney passenger tapping a contactless card on the in-car taxi terminal at the rear seat, with the takeaway 'Tap to pay. Never hand over the card.'

stacked.headline: The Sydney 'fake surge' that quotes A$145 for a A$55 ride.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Australia Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Sydney Airport Uber 'fake surge' scam: A$55 ride quoted at A$145 (2.7x)
stacked.pin_description: At Sydney Airport T1 and T2 rideshare bays, drivers circle and decline low fares so Uber escalates a 2.7x surge — quoting A$145-A$160 for a Darlinghurst ride that should be A$55. Compare DiDi and Bolt before ordering, or take Bus 400 / the airport train (~A$22 to Central). From the Tabiji Sydney Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Sydney Airport Uber fake-surge scam: a tourist opens Uber at the T1 rideshare bay expecting A$55, sees a 2.7x surge quoting A$145, drivers circle without accepting fares to manufacture scarcity, and the takeaway points to Bus 400 and the SYD airport train at A$22.

hook.hook: "2.7x surge" on a Tuesday afternoon. Walk to Bus 400.
hook.pin_title: Sydney Airport "2.7x surge" with no event is drivers gaming the queue
hook.pin_description: If Uber quotes A$145 with a 2.7x surge at Sydney Airport on a Tuesday, drivers are circling the bay and declining low fares to manufacture scarcity. Compare DiDi and Bolt — one is usually normal — or walk to Bus 400 to Bondi Junction. From Tabiji's Sydney scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at the Sydney Airport T1 rideshare bay holding a phone showing Uber quoting A$145 with a 2.7x surge multiplier on a clear afternoon.

lesson.lesson: Compare DiDi and Bolt before accepting Uber.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Sydney rule: compare DiDi and Bolt before accepting Uber
lesson.pin_description: DiDi and Bolt are less dominant at Sydney Airport so they surge less — one is usually priced normally when Uber spikes 2-3x. Bus 400 to Bondi Junction is a few dollars; the airport train to Central is ~A$22. Pre-book a hotel transfer if you arrive between 11pm-5am. More Sydney scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist at Sydney Airport with three rideshare apps open side by side comparing fares, with the takeaway 'Compare DiDi and Bolt before accepting Uber.'

stacked.headline: The Sydney 'Surry Hills studio' that costs A$1,260 and doesn't exist.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Australia Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Sydney fake Airbnb scam: A$1,260 bank transfer for a Surry Hills studio that isn't real
stacked.pin_description: Scammers clone Airbnb URLs for Surry Hills, CBD, Darlinghurst and Bondi listings, claiming 'platform fees' to push bank transfer. One Sydney visitor lost A$3,266 AUD on a fake working-holiday Airbnb. Always book via airbnb.com or booking.com — never a link in email. Funds in escrow only. From the Tabiji Sydney Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Sydney fake short-stay rental scam: a traveler finds a Surry Hills studio for A$180 a night on a cloned Airbnb page, the host claims platform fees inflate prices and asks for bank transfer of A$1,260 AUD, the address turns out to be someone else's home, and the takeaway points to the official Airbnb app.

hook.hook: "Bank-transfer direct to skip Airbnb fees." Hard no.
hook.pin_title: Sydney "bank-transfer to skip platform fees" lost one traveler A$3,266
hook.pin_description: If a Sydney 'Airbnb' host emails you a payment link asking for bank transfer to skip platform fees, the listing is cloned and you will lose the deposit. One working-holiday traveler lost A$3,266 to this exact pattern. Airbnb's fees are built into the displayed price. From Tabiji's Sydney scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Sydney 'host' email asking the traveler to bank-transfer A$1,260 AUD direct to skip Airbnb platform fees for a Surry Hills studio.

lesson.lesson: Pay only inside the app. Funds in escrow.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Sydney rental rule: pay only inside the app, funds in escrow
lesson.pin_description: Airbnb, Booking.com and Stayz hold your money in escrow and only release 24 hours after check-in. If you've already wired a Sydney 'host', call your bank within 24 hours — Australian banks can sometimes claw back funds before the recipient withdraws. More Sydney scams from Tabiji.

scams.scam_name: Bondi / Manly Beach Bag & Phone Theft

stacked.headline: The Sydney sand-line lift that empties your bag in one swipe.

stacked.pin_title: Bondi Beach bag theft: phone, wallet & passport gone during a 15-minute swim
stacked.pin_description: At Bondi, Manly and Coogee, thieves walk the towel line and scoop a phone off a sarong in one motion while you swim. Use the paid lockers at Bondi Pavilion (A$5-A$10), take a waterproof pouch in the water, or visit the beach in shifts. Leave the passport in the hotel safe. From the Tabiji Sydney Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of the Bondi Beach bag theft scam: a tourist drops a backpack on a towel and leaves a phone visible while going for a swim, a thief walks the towel line scooping the phone in one motion, the tourist returns to find the wallet and passport gone, and the takeaway points to the paid lockers at Bondi Pavilion.

hook.hook: "Aussies are friendly, nobody steals." They do.
hook.pin_title: Bondi sand-line: someone walking the towel line scoops a phone in one motion
hook.pin_description: Bondi, Manly and Coogee thieves are not dramatic street criminals — they walk the towel line at peak summer and lift a phone off a sarong in a single motion while you are 15 minutes into a swim. Use a waterproof pouch or the paid Bondi Pavilion locker. From Tabiji's Sydney scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a thief walking past beach towels at Bondi at peak summer, scooping a phone off a sarong in one motion as a tourist swims in the background.

lesson.lesson: Lockers, drybag, or shifts. Never bare sand.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Bondi beach rule: lockers, drybag, or shifts — never bare sand
lesson.pin_description: The paid lockers at Bondi Pavilion, Manly Surf Club and Coogee Pavilion are A$5-A$10. A A$20 drybag with a carabiner beats a tourist backpack. Carry only a bank card and a passport photocopy on the sand — leave the real one in the hotel safe. More Sydney scams from Tabiji.

stacked.headline: The Sydney A$22 paper ticket that should have been A$15.94.

stacked.pin_description: At Sydney Airport, Central and Circular Quay, a 'helpful' stranger pushes A$22 single-use paper tickets when a contactless tap is A$15.94 and Opal caps your day at A$18.40 weekdays / A$8.40 weekends. Always tap on AND off — even on buses and ferries to Manly. From the Tabiji Sydney Scam Survival Guide.
