hook.hook: "Just buy the paper ticket, it's easier." Don't.
hook.pin_title: Sydney "just buy the paper ticket" doubles your fare to A$22
hook.pin_description: At Sydney Airport station and Central, anyone steering you to a A$22 paper single-use ticket is costing you A$6 versus a contactless A$15.94 tap. Opal also caps the day at A$18.40 weekdays / A$8.40 weekends. Tap your bank card, not paper. From Tabiji's Sydney scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a stranger at the Sydney Airport station Opal machine pushing a confused tourist to buy an A$22 single-use paper ticket instead of tapping a contactless card.

lesson.lesson: Tap on. Tap off. Every ride.
lesson.foot: tabiji.ai  ·  Real scams from real travelers
lesson.pin_title: Sydney transport rule: tap on, tap off, every ride
lesson.pin_description: Forgetting to tap off a Sydney ferry at Manly or Watsons Bay charges the maximum A$17 fare. Tap with your contactless card on every train, bus, ferry and light rail and check the Opal Travel app for any max-fare mis-taps you can refund at a staffed station. More Sydney scams from Tabiji.
lesson.alt_text: Comic panel of a tourist tapping a contactless card off a ferry reader at Manly Wharf, with the takeaway 'Tap on. Tap off. Every ride.'

stacked.headline: The Sydney 'Twilight Climb' WhatsApp QR for cash that's already sold out.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Australia Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Sydney BridgeClimb scam: A$80-off 'Twilight Climb' WhatsApp QR is invalid at the gate

Taxi rank counters with a 'flat A$90 cash' quote on a A$52 metered fare. Take the Perth Airport train (under A$5, every 15 min) or wait 10 minutes for the surge to reset. hook.hook: "Flat A$90 cash, mate, meter's broken." Walk to the train.

hook.pin_description: If a Perth Airport taxi quotes a 'flat A$90 cash' to Northbridge or Perth CBD instead of running the meter, the actual metered fare is A$52 plus A$5 airport surcharge. Walk to the Perth Airport train at T3/T4 — under A$5 to the CBD, every 15 minutes. From Tabiji's Perth scam guide.

Wait 10 minutes for the surge to reset, or take the Perth Airport train (under A$5) to the CBD. More Perth scams from Tabiji.

stacked.pin_description: A Fremantle share-room on Facebook Marketplace at A$200/week with a 'landlord in Melbourne' asking for a A$400 bank-transfer deposit is the standard Perth fake — the address turns out to be a family home and the profile vanishes. Use flatmates.com.au, inspect in person, never pay before keys. From the Tabiji Perth Scam Survival Guide.

Use flatmates.com.au and viewing first. From Tabiji's Perth scam guide.

Use flatmates.com.au and the UWA accommodation board for sharehouses; airbnb.com or booking.com via the official app for short stays. Pay only after keys in hand. stacked.headline: The Canberra 'AFP arrest warrant' demanding A$1,400 by bank transfer.

stacked.pin_description: A caller posing as an Australian Federal Police officer says there's a warrant for your arrest over a visa violation but it can be cleared if you bank-transfer A$1,400 today. The AFP never demands payment by transfer, Bitcoin or gift cards. Hang up, call back via afp.gov.au, report to scamwatch.gov.au. From the Tabiji Canberra Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: "Bank transfer A$1,400 today or visa cancelled." Hang up.
hook.pin_title: Canberra AFP impersonation: 'transfer A$1,400 today or visa cancelled' is the script
hook.pin_description: Any caller claiming to be from the AFP, Services Australia, ATO, Border Force or Medicare and demanding immediate bank transfer, Bitcoin or gift cards is running the Canberra impersonation scam. No legitimate Australian agency ever takes payment that way. Hang up and call back via the official site. From Tabiji's Canberra scam guide.

lesson.pin_title: Canberra phone rule: hang up and call back via afp.gov.au

Hang up, call back the agency on the number from its official site (afp.gov.au, servicesaustralia.gov.au, ato.gov.au), and report to scamwatch.gov.au. If you've already paid, contact your bank within 24 hours. More Canberra scams from Tabiji.

stacked.pin_description: In Nov-May stinger season, dock-side operators sell 'exclusive stinger-free private beach experiences' at A$180 — usually a resort pool you could walk into for A$10 or the free public netted swim at Airlie Beach Lagoon. hook.pin_description: Airlie Beach Lagoon on the foreshore is free, stinger-netted in season and right in town. Hamilton Island Catseye Beach has a netted area at specific seasons. A A$10-15 stinger suit hire is included in most sailing and day-cruise operators. Skip A$180 'exclusive' beach pitches. From Tabiji's Whitsundays scam guide.

hook.pin_description: On the Quicksilver Agincourt Reef pontoon, the A$175 'Ocean Walk' helmet dive is an optional onboard upsell — Quicksilver's base cruise is fine, but TripAdvisor reviews call the helmet add-on a low-delivery fee. stacked.headline: The Port Douglas A$265 taxi quote when the shuttle is A$58-75.

stacked.pin_description: At Cairns Airport (CNS) drivers quote A$265 for the Port Douglas private transfer when Sun Palm Transport, Exemplar Coaches and CaPTA run the same 60-minute drive at A$58-75. Pre-book the shuttle before you fly — drivers meet you at arrivals with a sign. Uber is the A$100-140 fallback. From the Tabiji Port Douglas Scam Survival Guide.

stacked.headline: The Port Douglas A$28 menu salad that bills as A$38 with stacked surcharges.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Australia Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Port Douglas Macrossan Street: A$28 menu salad bills as A$38 with surcharges
stacked.pin_description: Macrossan Street outdoor tables can stack a A$5 'outdoor seat' surcharge, a 15% weekend surcharge and an undisclosed 'cover charge' onto a A$28 menu salad — the bill arrives at A$38. Queensland surcharges are legal only if disclosed on the menu. Check menu prices inside, decline tip prompts. From the Tabiji Port Douglas Scam Survival Guide.

hook.hook: "That's the outdoor seat surcharge." Check the menu inside.
hook.pin_title: Macrossan Street: A$28 menu, A$38 bill — surcharges hidden inside
hook.pin_description: On Macrossan Street if your outdoor-seat bill is A$10 over the menu price with a 'cover charge' you weren't shown, Queensland law lets you refuse undisclosed surcharges. Check menu prices inside before sitting outside, and decline 15-20% card-reader tip prompts — staff are paid full wage. From Tabiji's Port Douglas scam guide.

scams.scam_name: Great Barrier Reef 'Outer Reef' Tour Bait & Switch
scams.location: Port Douglas Marina booking booths, Macrossan Street agents

stacked.headline: The Port Douglas A$120 'Great Barrier Reef' tour that's an inner-reef sand cay.
stacked.brand_sub: From the Australia Scam Survival Guide
stacked.pin_title: Port Douglas reef scam: A$120 'outer reef' is Low Isles inner-reef cay
stacked.pin_description: Macrossan Street agents sell 'Great Barrier Reef outer-reef full-day' at A$120 — the boat goes to Low Isles, an inner-reef sand cay 15 km offshore, not the outer reef. Real outer-reef trips with Quicksilver, Wavedancer, Poseidon or Calypso run A$220-330. Specify Agincourt, Tongue or Ribbon Reefs in writing. From the Tabiji Port Douglas Scam Survival Guide.
stacked.alt_text: Four-panel comic of a Port Douglas Great Barrier Reef bait-and-switch on Macrossan Street: an agent sells a 'Great Barrier Reef outer reef full-day' for A$120, on the day the boat heads to Low Isles inner-reef sand cay 15 km offshore with 3-5 metre visibility, the actual outer reef at Agincourt is 90 minutes further out, and the takeaway names Quicksilver, Wavedancer, Poseidon and Calypso as outer-reef operators.

hook.hook: "Outer reef full-day, A$120." Ask for the site name.
hook.pin_title: Port Douglas 'A$120 outer reef' is a Low Isles inner-reef switch
hook.pin_description: If a Macrossan Street agent quotes 'Great Barrier Reef outer-reef full-day' at A$120-160 and won't name Agincourt, Tongue or Ribbon Reefs in writing, you're booking inner-reef Low Isles. Outer-reef certified runs are A$220-330. Cash-only no-receipt is the giveaway. From Tabiji's Port Douglas scam guide.
hook.alt_text: Comic panel of a Macrossan Street agent in Port Douglas pitching 'Great Barrier Reef outer reef A$120 full-day' to a couple while reaching for cash, the receipt book noticeably absent.
